goal.request: Apply the researched natural-environment visual semantics and candidate data, then independently test five random complex concepts with one attached appearance reference and one image generation attempt per arm.

evidence.claim: Twelve relational environment grammars produced 75 candidate records, 12 mixins, and 8 still-image hard profiles with observable and non-inference boundaries.
The natural-environment scope passes focused routing, dictionary, retrieval, index, and scene-expression checks.
All five randomly assigned terms map to exactly one intended mixin and all expected current candidate IDs after each core is frozen.
Five built-in one-shot images pass all 25 target environment gates; shared gates pass 24 of 25 and the strict full randomized scenarios pass 3 of 5.

hypotheses.statement: Component-plus-relation contracts preserve natural-environment meaning in complex referenced photographs better than broad scenery labels.
hypotheses.falsifier: Any sampled image loses one required environment component or substitutes a confound while still being marked pass.

hypotheses.statement: A visible reference-guided adult can be integrated without hiding the environment and while remaining facially readable.
hypotheses.falsifier: Any arm either hides a target component or loses reference-appearance readability at a required scale.

decision.rationale: The natural-environment representation is pixel-qualified on all five sampled profiles, but the complete reference-integrated qualification remains partial because arm-03 loses observable facial continuity and arm-02 loses a randomized secondary action. No rerender was used to hide either failure.
